scenarios.title: Overload changes 'target' to 'each'
decisions: A casts Mizzium Mortars for its overload cost {3}{R}{R}{R}, tapping all six Mountains; no targets are chosen.
Both players pass; Mizzium Mortars resolves.

variants.label: overloaded
variants.expected: Mizzium Mortars deals 4 damage to each creature A does not control. Hill Giant and Grizzly Bears are destroyed and go to B's graveyard. Runeclaw Bear is unharmed.

variants.label: normal_cast
variants.delta: A casts Mizzium Mortars for {1}{R} (tapping two Mountains) targeting Hill Giant instead of paying the overload cost.
variants.expected: Mizzium Mortars deals 4 damage to Hill Giant only, which is destroyed. Grizzly Bears has no damage; Runeclaw Bear is unharmed.

scenarios.title: An overloaded spell has no targets and can affect objects that could not be targeted
decisions: A casts Mizzium Mortars for its overload cost {3}{R}{R}{R}, tapping all six Mountains; no targets are chosen.
If the cast is legal, both players pass and Mizzium Mortars resolves.

variants.label: overloaded
variants.expected: The cast is legal because the spell requires no targets. Mizzium Mortars deals 4 damage to Gladecover Scout (hexproof), which is destroyed and goes to B's graveyard.

variants.label: normal_cast
variants.delta: A tries to cast Mizzium Mortars for {1}{R} targeting Gladecover Scout instead of paying the overload cost.
variants.expected: The cast is illegal: Gladecover Scout has hexproof and is the only creature A does not control, so Mizzium Mortars has no legal target and cannot be cast.
